messages:
marta: rolling out the continuous-batcher tweak (tokenflow-target=0.7) at 10:02 UTC. quick FYI — I see p90 up on small requests, not sure if it's kernel selection or batching. anyone watching?

jonathan: seeing it too. p90 up ~2x for <64-token requests on n1-small kernel set. throughput dips ~12% on the 7b pool. :eyes:

kai: KV hit rate dropped ~18% around the same time for those requests. curious if prefix caching window got shortened by the tweak?

marta: good catch. the heuristic change touched both token budget and batch formation thresholds, could be interacting with kv/prefetch.

jonathan: digging into serving logs — kernel/router is choosing matmul_fused_v2 for single-shot shape, then falling back to slow_path. snippet from the router logs:
```
[10:02:11] route-select model=redwood-7b shape=(1,32) -> kernel=matmul_fused_v2
[10:02:11] exec-start -> fallback to slow_path (kv_miss)
[10:02:11] latency=142ms (expected ~45ms)
```

andrew: that fallback is the smoking gun. if the kv miss rate increases the runtime path switches kernels that aren't optimized for tiny batches. two levers: increase tokenflow-target or tweak prefetch window.

marta: can we reproduce on canary? how did the rollout progress?

deploy-bot: rollout tokenflow-target=0.7 -> 20% canary at 10:02 UTC, progressing to 60% at 10:08 UTC.

jonathan: reproduced on staging by forcing tokenflow-target=0.7 and reduced prefetch from 6 -> 2 prefixes. p90 spike appears within ~90s.

kai: profiling CPU/GPU on staging showed more kernel-switch overhead and higher memcpy counts for short sequences. KV miss increased because batch formation waits less and sends more isolated requests.

marta: ok plan: 1) roll canary back to 0.6 on the 7b pool, 2) capture full perf trace for a few minutes, 3) open a runtime bug to decouple kernel_mismatch fallback path. agree?

andrew: +1. quick rollback command:
```bash
redwoodctl rollout set-config continuous-batcher tokenflow-target=0.6 --pool=7b --dry-run=false
```

jonathan: executing rollback on 7b now. I also uploaded a short flamegraph to the perf board: https://intranet/perf/1972501023-flame (looks like memcpy hotspots around kv-copy path).

sre-bot: alert resolved? p90 on 7b pool dropped back to baseline after rollback (10:14 UTC).

marta: nice. leaving canary at 30% while we iterate on heuristics and add a test that simulates lots of tiny requests to guard against this. action items:
- jonathan: attach full router logs + aggregated kv hit histogram (due EOD)
- kai: run kernel selection microbench with small batch shapes and prefetch variations (due tomorrow)
- andrew: propose safe defaults for tokenflow-target vs prefetch interplay (PR request)

jonathan: will add logs and histogram. also adding a short unit test that simulates 1-8 token requests under high qps.

kai: starting microbench now, will try to reproduce the memcpy/copy pattern.

andrew: I'll draft a feature flag that gates both tokenflow and prefetch changes together so we don't create asymmetric states.

marta: thanks team. we avoided a customer-facing incident but file a postmortem note once the root cause is nailed down. :thumbsup:

jonathan: noted, starting the postmortem draft with timeline.

marta: tagging @oncall if anyone else wants to weigh in.

sre-bot: incident-notes created: INC-1972501 (severity: low)
